segments.title: Cold Open & Station Sign-On
segments.notes: Pepito delivers top-of-hour sign-on, announces truncated Thursday runtime before Patreon, teases Kendelle job news.

segments.title: SpaceX IPO Filing Analysis
segments.notes: Anchor and science correspondent dissect S-1 filing: $1.75T target valuation, 85.1% Musk voting control, $18.67B revenue vs $4.94B loss, orbital supercomputing and asteroid mining growth claims.

segments.title: Wrestling Speculation: Triple H & Vince McMahon
segments.notes: Case predicts Triple H congressional run in early 2030s, Vince McMahon return to wrestling TV before death for crowd adulation.

segments.title: Hype Train Interruption Attempt
segments.notes: Hype Train triggers over Westside Gunn beats but fails to drop a beat; talked over by anchor and EP.

segments.title: Chat News Rapid Fire
segments.notes: Headlines: Trump son quote, Texas kangaroo, Jeff Probst Survivor spoiler, depression-detection video game, FWC biologist $400K settlement over Charlie Kirk post.

segments.title: Final Fantasy Villain Debate: Kefka vs Sephiroth
segments.notes: Crum defends Kefka's maniacal harlequin design; Munch champions Sephiroth as definitive J-pop antagonist; devolves into 'all villains are tall with long swords' taxonomy including Chucky, Freddy Krueger, Negan.

segments.title: Aladdin Activity Center Gameplay
segments.notes: Brandon plays 1990s edutainment title amid muffled-door maternal interventions: cousin 'trout' prison nail-file cake, Pastor Joe house blessing, cockroach-infested chicken tenders.

segments.title: Raid & Sign-Off
segments.notes: Case raids 'doctor buggerly dank' (mispronounced), promises longer stream tomorrow, ends for Patreon.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: executive producer. Delivers station sign-on, manages truncated Thursday runtime, teases Kendelle job exit.

characters.name: Case Blackwell
characters.notes: anchor. Navigates SpaceX financials, wrestling predictions, chat headlines, and segment transitions before Patreon handoff.

characters.name: Chet (Chet Manscape)
characters.notes: science correspondent. Commandeers news desk to riff on orbital data centers, space cooling physics, and Disney's Wish as market philosophy.

characters.name: Crum
characters.notes: debate analyst. Defends Kefka as superior Final Fantasy villain against Munch's Sephiroth advocacy.

characters.name: Munch
characters.notes: debate analyst. Champions Sephiroth as definitive antagonist while derailing into universal tall-villain taxonomy.

characters.name: Brandon (CryptoZeu$)
characters.notes: gaming correspondent. Plays Aladdin Activity Center under maternal siege and pastoral interference.

characters.name: Hype Train
characters.notes: musical interrupter. Attempts freestyle over Westside Gunn beats but fails to drop beat before being talked over.

characters.name: Brandon's Mom
characters.notes: muffled-door antagonist. Delivers cousin prison updates, nail-file cake lore, and Pastor Joe spiritual advisories through bedroom door.

lore_notes.fact: SpaceX files Form S-1 for Nasdaq listing under ticker SPCX targeting $1.75T valuation with Elon Musk retaining 85.1% voting control.
SpaceX 2025 financials show $18.67B revenue (33.2% YoY growth) against $4.94B net loss, continuing multi-year operating losses.
IPO filing reveals SpaceX targeting orbital supercomputing, asteroid mining, and extraterrestrial logistics as growth vectors.
Case sets reminder to apply for unspecified 'part' (sub goal) at 11am next day.
Case predicts Triple H runs for Congress in early 2030s; Vince McMahon returns to wrestling TV before death for crowd adulation.
Brandon's mother reveals cousin 'trout' incarcerated until 2069, receives birthday card with nail file baked into cake.
Brandon's mother identifies 'Pastor Joe' as spiritual advisor who 'blesses the house' over Brandon's art.
Case references three-minute depression-detection video game from earlier chat headline.

episode_summary: Barely Informed News dissected SpaceX's $1.75 trillion IPO filing revealing orbital data center ambitions amid $5 billion annual losses, then pivoted to wrestling speculation before a Munch & Crum debate on Final Fantasy villainy devolved into a taxonomy of tall antagonists. The broadcast concluded with CryptoZeu$ speedrunning Aladdin Activity Center under maternal siege while Hype Train's freestyle attempt collapsed into beatless noise ahead of a Patreon handoff.
